scope: Sources establish terms or documented usage. Pixel gates and candidate decompositions are project proposals, not statements of universal standards. No reference images were downloaded or qualified.

sources.title: Why Do Artists Use Contrapposto?
sources.supports: Loaded leg, relaxed free leg and counterbalance; example-specific arm positions are not universal requirements.

sources.title: Figura serpentinata
sources.supports: Spiralling about a central axis with different lower- and upper-body directions; not a synonym for a projected S curve.

sources.title: Recognizing the Gods
sources.supports: Tribhanga, religious hand gestures and seated iconographic forms in their particular cultural contexts; local comparisons do not make all contrapposto and tribhanga synonymous.

sources.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e: Types of Body Movements
sources.supports: Joint-specific flexion/extension, rotation, elevation/depression, protraction/retraction, dorsiflexion/plantarflexion and other movement pairs; not instructions for an individual's range of motion.

sources.title: Sitting Poses
sources.supports: Seated variants, leg configurations, edge sitting and chair/floor interactions; examples are photographic conventions rather than mandatory forms.

sources.title: A Peek Inside the Boudoir with Cherie Steinberg
sources.supports: Prone/supine arrangements and pointed feet in a boudoir workflow; genre also depends on lighting, framing and styling, not a unique skeleton.

sources.title: Tips for effective hand poses and sitting poses
sources.supports: Hand placement, gentle versus pressing contact, props and camera-relative foreshortening; recommendations are choices rather than universal aesthetic laws.

sources.title: Posing tip: check wrists and hands
sources.supports: Wrist shape can vary independently of where a hand touches; camera angle affects its visible line.

sources.title: Squinch
sources.supports: Named eye-area posing direction distinct from shutting the eyes or a generic smile; perceived confidence is an intended impression, not an inferred personal trait.

sources.title: Smize usage, 2012
sources.supports: Historical use of smile-with-the-eyes terminology; not proof of a single measurable geometry or a current trend.

sources.title: 핫한 브이, 2022
sources.supports: Camera-directed, palm-up V variant called gyaru peace; broad generational labels must not become exact pose aliases.

sources.title: What Is the Bambi Pose? 2017
sources.supports: A low kneeling/heel-sitting variant with thighs over shins; tall kneeling is a meaningful negative control. Other communities can use variants.

sources.title: Barbie feet, 2018
sources.supports: Barefoot raised-heel posing usage, including different body arrangements; not equivalent to ballet pointe or wearing high heels.

sources.title: How To Slay in Every Selfie with T-Rex Hands, 2016
sources.supports: Practitioner use of the T-Rex-hands nickname. Exact finger/wrist variant still requires a chosen visual reference.

sources.title: 2018 Beauty Moments: migraine pose
sources.supports: Forehead-hand posing nickname in a satirical historical article; no actual headache or medical condition can be inferred.

sources.title: Forget Fish Gape! The Newest Selfie Trick Is..., 2015
sources.supports: Sparrow-face/fish-gape/hair-twirl usage with partially overlapping descriptions; weak labels need variant definitions, not forced synonyms.

sources.title: Cheek-heart photo caption referenced by original conversation
sources.supports: Lead only. No claim that this image or its finger geometry was verified.

sources.title: How To Take Model Digitals
sources.supports: Digitals are a casting-image set with restrained presentation and several views; the label alone does not determine one pose or imply film capture.

sources.title: Engagement Photo Poses
sources.supports: Side-by-side, back-to-front, handholding and specified facial contact; relationship labels are not needed for geometry.

sources.title: The Thinker (Le Penseur), visual description
sources.supports: Object-specific right elbow on left knee, chin on right hand and twisted seated body; generic chin-rest does not establish the Rodin arrangement.

sources.title: Panel of Venus Pudica
sources.supports: A particular standing pudica arrangement and arm covering; not every self-covering pose belongs to this iconography.

sources.title: Guanyin seated in royal ease
sources.supports: Raised leg and casually draped arm in rajalilasana. Generic open failed on re-fetch; search returned the museum's description. Do not conflate all lalitasana variants.

sources.title: Ballet Terms and Positions
sources.supports: Arabesque, attitude, croisé, grand jeté and pointe distinctions. School-specific arm forms and angles remain variants.

sources.title: Ballet Terms P
sources.supports: Passé as passing movement; plié and port de bras. A still frame cannot prove an entire transition.

sources.title: Ballet Terms R
sources.supports: Retiré bent working leg with foot near support knee; relevé raising onto pointe/demi-pointe with technique variants.

sources.title: Ballet Terms E
sources.supports: Effacé versus croisé is viewer-relative openness/crossing. It must not be encoded as a generic body angle alone.

sources.title: A Brief History of Voguing
sources.supports: Ballroom origins and different voguing styles. Genre and movement families do not provide a unique still-image pose; no photographed identity inference.

sources.title: Crane (Crow) Pose
sources.supports: Bent-arm Crow (Kakasana) and straighter-arm Crane (Bakasana) distinction in this teaching convention; names vary by school.

sources.title: Comprehensive Yoga Poses Finder
sources.supports: Standing/seated/prone/supine pose families and Sanskrit names. Index includes naming variants such as Gomukhasana as Cow Pose and a lying twist as Natarajasana; never copy aliases without checking geometry. Individual pages remain to be checked for several draft atoms.

sources.title: Dancer Pose
sources.supports: Natarajasana as a standing balance/backbend with lifted leg; distinct from the lying twist in another index.

sources.title: Extended Side-Angle Pose Explainer
sources.supports: Utthita Parsvakonasana diagonal extension connecting grounded rear leg, side body and overhead arm; anterior knee bends, unlike basic straight-legged triangle.

sources.title: Official Bodybuilding Rules
sources.supports: Eight listed mandatory poses and separate quarter-turn comparison. Evidence is scoped to the page's bodybuilding division; not all organizations or divisions.

sources.title: M字開脚 usage in a photo-book announcement, 2023
sources.supports: Lexical occurrence of M字開脚 in adult editorial context; no standardized knee/foot/seat geometry established by text alone.

sources.title: 女豹ポーズ photo caption, 2019
sources.supports: Lexical usage only; the linked photograph was not inspected or classified. Do not treat all quadruped forms as the same variant.

sources.title: Fan Dance
sources.supports: Fan dance involves movement, travelling, expression and choreography; fan position/occlusion/gesture are separate still-frame properties.

sources.title: How to Draw Dynamic Poses and Movement
sources.supports: Line of action, gravity, viewpoint and gestures in illustration. Photo pose validation must independently check actual support/contact and should not copy exaggerated drawing conventions as anatomy rules.

sources.title: AAT contrapposto record 300067391
sources.supports: Terminological scope: asymmetrical but balanced figure with differently tipped or turned body axes; cross-check with loaded/free-leg interpretation rather than treating arbitrary bend as contrapposto.

sources.title: 虫歯ポーズ usage, 2020
sources.supports: Existence of the nickname in posed screenshot context. This text does not prove one standardized hand-to-cheek geometry or an actual dental condition.

sources.title: Ballet Terms A
sources.supports: Arabesque on one leg with the other extended backward; attitude has a bent lifted working leg. Arm placement remains variant-specific.

sources.title: Ballet Terms D
sources.supports: Demi-pointe support on balls/underside of toes versus full toe-tip pointe. This page does not contain a développé entry.

sources.title: Ballet Vocab: Battement Tendu
sources.supports: Tendu foot articulation and weight placement; related Glissé description explicitly says the extended foot leaves the floor. The grounded versus lifted contrast informs the proposed gate; subscriber video was not viewed.

sources.title: Ballet Vocab: Développé
sources.supports: Public teacher-led course description defines développé as unfolding. Selected leg direction and exact transition require variant/reference review; subscriber video was not viewed.

access_notes.note: No authentication URLs, nonces or tokens are retained. Use accessible school sources and check individual definitions before promotion.
